# A center of one limb times a power of two, and whether it is exact

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bv_mul_pow2_step_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x c$, exact when $x c = 0$ or $\lvert x c\rvert > \frac{\eta}{2u}$; and the mask $e$, true exactly when those conditions hold:

$$z \approx x c.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_mul_pow2_1`, called by `ldexp` and `half` of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $c$ is a power of two: $c = 2^n$ for an integer $n$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z = \mathrm{RN}(x c)$: the number of the format nearest to $x c$, ties to even.
- $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$; and $z = x c$ exactly when $x c = 0$ or $\lvert x c\rvert > \frac{\eta}{2u}$; $e$ is true exactly when $x c = 0$ or $\lvert x c\rvert > \frac{\eta}{2u}$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1075} \approx 2.4703 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-150} \approx 7.0065 \times 10^{-46}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bv_mul_pow2_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BvPow2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BvPow2.v), against `bv_mul_pow2_step_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_mul_pow2_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bv_mul_pow2_step_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x c : R,
  fmt emin prec x ->
  fmt emin prec c ->
  (exists n : Z, c = bpow radix2 n) ->
  let '(z, e) := bv_mul_pow2_step_1 emin prec tie_even x c in
  fmt emin prec z /\
  z = RN emin prec (x * c) /\
  Rabs (z - (x * c)) <= (1 / 2) * eta emin /\
  (((x * c) = 0 \/ (eta emin / (2 * u prec)) < Rabs (x * c)) ->
   z = (x * c)) /\
  (e = true <-> ((x * c) = 0 \/ (eta emin / (2 * u prec)) < Rabs (x * c))).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `bv_mul_pow2_step_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** mul_pow2_step_1 on the center, and the exactness of the center of ball_mul_pow2_1 (milestone2.md, BallVector). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_mul_pow2_step_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_mul_pow2_step_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The step of bv_mul_pow2_1, a BallVector with one-limb centers times a positive power of two c
# (milestone2.md, "BallVector": bv_mul_pow2_k, "the same kernel along the entries, with ec true only
# when it is for every entry"): the center scaled as mul_pow2_step_1 does, and as a second output the
# mask ec of ball_mul_pow2_1, that this entry's scaling is exact: the scaled center above the smallest
# normal number N = eta / (2u) in magnitude, or the center zero. The ball vector ands it over the
# entries into a mask of its state, which its radius takes. The mask is true exactly when the
# condition of exact_when holds (exact_flag): a product by a power of two above N in magnitude is a
# number of the format, so its rounding is above N exactly when it is. The center is stored (written
# through Kairn) and only multiplied; the program gives c, which is only multiplied (rule R3).

z  = prod(x, c)
am = abs(z)
bc = lt(const up(eta/(2*u)), am)
zc = eq(x, 0)
e  = or(bc, zc)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#bv_mul_pow2_step_1)).

**These runs judged other claims.** They judged `rounded(z) nearest`; `error(z) form R, c=0, k=1, t=1/2, exact when (x*c = 0 or |x*c| > eta/(2*u)), exact_flag e`; the kernel now claims `rounded(z) nearest`; `error(z) form R, c=0, k=1, t=1/2`. Their numbers are not about the statement above.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 96 796 926 | 0 | 1 | yes |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 97 149 546 | 0 | 1 | yes |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 274 879 | 0 | 1 (`fp:8:-14:6`) | yes |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
